title: Watari et al. (2019), native main article; DOI 10.3354/meps12508
supports: Verified 12-page focal PDF, including JSTOR cover. Sections 2.2/2.3: PDF 4/printed 297; Table 1: PDF 5/298 group identities; Table 2: PDF 6/299 scalars and numeric/censored/dash Landings; Table 3: PDF 8/301 diet. One linked 2013 OYC/KC/OF model has 41 source groups; the selected 39-group detritus experiment is separate.

title: Publisher Supplement 1: authentic indexed text, partially retained
supports: Authentic title/authors/DOI verified in the retained web-reader return for m12508_supp.pdf. Only readable pages 1–11 were retained, although the tool reports 46 pages. S1 sections 4/5/7 name blue shark, four Thunnus, swordfish, dolphinfish and Brama; section 3 reports no 2013 seabird catch. Direct routes currently return 404/401; exact PDF bytes and later S1 membership/time-series remain unavailable.

title: Sea Around Us LME 49 v50.1 catch and organism provenance
supports: Original reported/unreported catch archive, downloaded 3 September 2026, covers 1950–2019. Landings and discards are disjoint catch-type components; total catch is not counted twice. Every one of 253 exact labels is included, even with zero reference catch. Raw reporting/functional metadata supports ecology but does not define exhaustive model membership.

title: Protected independent trophic levels and simple-chain coefficients
supports: Classic PPR / Taxa retains 229 coefficients, trophic levels and provenance independently of model TL. Reference PPR uses saved wet coefficient × 2019 landings / 9 once. The 24 missing coefficients/TLs all have zero 2019 landings and zero annual PPR; coefficient/TL remains unknown. No generic TL substitution.

title: WoRMS primary exact-name API: 257 retained queries
supports: Reviewed 1 October 2026. All 253 catch labels and four source names were queried exactly; four residual reporting concepts have no formal taxon record. Responses retain rank, family, accepted name and primary URL. Theragra chalcogramma → Gadus chalcogrammus and Sardinops melanostictus → Sardinops sagax are verified. Identity/rank does not observe regional catch composition.

title: FishBase synonym 1477: Japanese sardine melanostictus → sagax
supports: Primary synonym record identifies Sardinops melanostictus as a junior synonym of S. sagax; the species summary identifies the Japanese lineage (melanostictus). This bridges exact source group 9. The global common name South American pilchard is not interpreted as caught geography.

title: Exact provider reporting keys and independent catch reconstruction
supports: Local residual key 100039 is marine bony fish and 100339 pelagic bony fish, under ISSCAAP 39 / Osteichthyes. Elasmobranchii excludes chimaeras; Chondrichthyes includes them. Provider common names and functional fields are retained. Functional tags support ecology without defining exhaustive taxonomic membership.

title: All eligible/rejected groups and complete catch/biomass vectors
supports: Table 2 Landings/export uses t/km² of total model area/year; B uses t/km² of total model area. Each candidate retains raw numeric/censored/missing catch, loaded catch, complete biomass, totals and weight. Use complete catch first, otherwise complete whole-domain biomass at Medium confidence. No second 0.2/0.2/0.6 habitat weighting. Fixed 2013 proxies transfer across all years and bases.

title: Accepted pooled-detritus experiment and runtime provenance
supports: Historical selection/provenance, not the current mapping inventory. Source detritus 9.58 + 6.04 + 28.50 = 44.12; all 35 consumers and three spatial phytoplankton pools remain unchanged. Missing/censored inputs, 83 normalized diet cells, 299 scalar completions, seabird B=1/PB=QB=0, GS defaults, solved BA and full-retention routing remain protected limitations.

title: Full GE, TE and Egestion basal-source matrices
supports: All 40 recipients × five basal sources × three options = 600 finite entries inspected, including unfished Seabirds and computational import 40. Saved method coefficients match scoped column sums. Four negative TE pairings retain TE FAIL; GE/Egestion threshold OK both retain strict balance false. Full configuration/direct returns retained; no new solver or MC run.

title: Original Figure 1 calibrated footprint and target overlap
supports: Native Figure 1, PDF 3/printed 296: colored KC/OYC/OF water pools, calibrated to the graticule and checked with fourteen water/land controls. Approximate A 30–36%, B 49–51%, Low confidence. Prose 30–50°N/150°E encloses the study but is not a full rectangle. Published 913,102 km² is separate from the graphical trace. No geographic catch/PPR multiplier.

title: Method-specific contributions under reference controls
supports: 2019 landings; all source scope/all taxa/no group filter/unidentified method. Retains each taxon coefficient and contribution, plus largest contributors, independently of the classic confidence PPR denominator. Very low GE/TE/Egestion exposure shares differ. Provisional TE arithmetic does not remove FAIL or admit production.

title: FAO (2002), Western Central Atlantic guide: octopod habitats
supports: Primary readable PDF, reviewed 1 October 2026. PDF 2/printed 217 describes pelagic Argonautidae; PDF 4–5/219–220 distinguishes benthic Octopodidae from pelagic families, while noting some planktonic paralarvae. Supports separate order versus family/genus habitat analogies. Does not observe caught stages or reveal Watari later S1 membership.

title: FAO (1990), Gulf of Guinea guide: Sepia/Sepiella accounts
supports: Primary readable PDF, reviewed 1 October 2026. PDF 3–5/printed 195–197 supports benthic/demersal adult cuttlefish traits. PDF 6/198 reports pelagic-trawl Heteroteuthis dispar with habitat unknown and distinguishes demersal bobtails. These are trait analogues, not Gulf of Guinea catch transfers, verified Japanese occurrence or Watari membership. Caught composition remains unknown.

title: FAO (2005), Cephalopods of the World, vol. 1: adult bobtail ecology
supports: Primary readable PDF, reviewed 1 October 2026. PDF 2/printed 199: adult Heteroteuthis dispar in lower epipelagic/mesopelagic water, commonly 200–300 m, caught by pelagic nets/trawlers. PDF 3/200: Stoloteuthis leucoptera at 160–700 m, potentially upper mesopelagic. Supports broad provider Sepiida connection to 27/28. Global traits do not prove Watari Japanese occurrence, S1 membership or caught proportions.
